title: Bayesian Predictive Geometry (BPG) for Dynamical Systems
abstract: This paper introduces Bayesian Predictive Geometry (BPG), a novel computational framework for dynamically generating and refining geometric representations of complex dynamical systems. Traditional geometric analysis often falls short in accurately modeling evolving systems due to limitations in handling non-linearity and inherent uncertainty. BPG addresses these challenges by extending Bayesian inference to encompass the entire trajectory of a system, modeling non-linearity, and incorporating probabilistic geometric modeling. The core mechanism involves constructing a probabilistic geometric model that evolves the system's geometry in real-time, allowing for improved long-term simulations and prediction of emergent behavior. This work demonstrates the efficacy of BPG through a series of illustrative examples and quantitative analysis, showcasing its potential to significantly enhance the accuracy and efficiency of dynamical system simulations.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Entropy Adaptive Computation Model
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers the potential for unprecedented computational capabilities. This research explores the utilization of quantum entanglement to enhance information processing and measurement, specifically focusing on the accurate quantification of quantum entanglement information entropy. We propose a novel computational model leveraging entangled states to achieve precise measurement and computation, ultimately aiming to improve the efficiency and security of quantum computations. The study will highlight the integration of quantum entanglement with existing computational methods to address limitations in current quantum computing paradigms. The core claim is that the proposed model offers a significant advancement in the measurement and entropy computation of quantum entanglement, contributing to a more robust and efficient quantum system.

title: The identity component of a Jacobian lens inflates the noise floor computed from it
abstract: A transformer's residual stream adds each layer's output to what came before, so the corpus-averaged Jacobian lens J = E[dh_final/dh_l] contains a copy of the identity by construction, and its share grows with depth as less transformation remains above the layer: at the deepest fitted layer of the six lenses read here from models above 1B parameters it is 66% to 88% of the matrix. That matters for any spectral read whose threshold is derived from the frame it is judging. A finite-size Marchenko-Pastur / Tracy-Widom edge estimates its variance as a de-biased median row energy, and an added alpha*I contributes alpha^2 to every row -- the one contribution a median over rows cannot reject -- so the identity raises the floor computed from it by more than 2x on eight of the ten lenses and by up to 4.8x, and the modes in between fall under the line. Separating the two is exact and closed form: alpha = tr(J)/d is the orthogonal projection of J onto span(I) under the Frobenius inner product, a trace and a subtraction with no threshold in it. Reading J - alpha*I in place of J changes the resolved count by 2x to 21x across all eleven lens files read - ten of the twenty-two on the Neuronpedia mirror - in 9 of 10 models, five families, widths 512 to 4096. Most of that range is not a property of transformers: two structure-free surrogates measure the part that belongs to the transport, differing in whether the floor's own variance input (a median row energy) is held fixed: one redraws both subspaces at fixed spectrum and alpha, the other rotates at fixed spectrum, alpha and every row norm, preserved to 2e-16. The excess attributable to the transport lies between 1.15x and 1.87x, and the correlation with identity share behaves the same way on the surrogates (+0.745 real, +0.758 and +0.657 surrogate). The directions below the raw read's floor are reproducible: across the two independent fits of Qwen3.5-4B they name the same vocabulary at Jaccard 0.390, against 0.038 for random directions decoded through the same readout. That agreement decays as a smooth power law in mode index with no knee at the floor, so it establishes that reproducible structure extends well past the raw count rather than that it stops at the residual one. Below relative depth 0.6 the two reads agree. Built on the Entroptics instrument, which it consumes as an engine rather than reimplementing. Includes the paper, the implementation, and the experiments that reproduce every figure from published lens files.

title: ##基于情感反馈的程序学习
abstract: This paper explores the novel approach of leveraging human emotional feedback to guide the learning process of programs. Traditional program learning often relies solely on objective metrics, which may not always align with human preferences or needs. This work proposes a framework where emotional responses, such as satisfaction or confusion, are utilized as dynamic feedback signals. Specifically, we construct an emotion-aware system that captures user sentiment in real-time. This sentiment data is then incorporated into reinforcement learning algorithms, either as reward signals or loss functions, effectively steering the program's development toward outputs that elicit desired emotional responses. We argue that this approach represents a significant advancement in program learning, offering the potential to create systems that are more intuitive, adaptable, and ultimately, more useful to humans. The core claim centers around the improved alignment of program behavior with human needs through the inclusion of emotional data. This paper details the proposed methodology, focusing on the construction of the emotion-aware system and its integration with reinforcement learning. ---

title: Adaptive Quantum Error Correction via Machine Learning
abstract: Quantum error correction (QEC) is critical for the reliable implementation of quantum computers, but current QEC protocols often rely on fixed parameters and struggle to adapt to fluctuating environmental noise. This work proposes a novel approach to QEC that leverages machine learning (ML) to dynamically adapt the parameters of QEC protocols in real-time. The core idea involves training neural networks to predict error rates based on observed quantum data and subsequently optimizing the error correction strategies. This adaptive framework offers the potential for significantly improved performance and resilience against evolving noise characteristics. The primary focus is on the theoretical framework and algorithm design, without the need for experimental validation. The proposed method represents a shift from static QEC to a more flexible and efficient system, addressing a key limitation in current quantum computing architectures. The key concept is represented by the following equation: εt = f(xt, θt, η), where εt is the error rate at time *t*, xt is the quantum state at time *t*, θt are the parameters of the QEC protocol at time *t*, and η is the learning rate. This equation highlights the adaptive nature of the system. The efficiency of the system is measured by the reduction in error rates achieved through adaptive parameter adjustment. Further analysis includes the concept of a cost function, C(θ), that represents the overall error correction performance. The goal is to minimize this cost function using the trained neural network. The core of the system relies on a feedback loop – the neural network predicts the error rate, which then influences the adjustment of the QEC protocol parameters.

title: Dimensional Matching Quantum Algorithm
abstract: This paper introduces a novel quantum algorithm, the Dimensional Matching Quantum Algorithm (DMQA), designed to efficiently identify optimal matchings within multi-dimensional spaces. Leveraging quantum entanglement, DMQA aims to surpass classical algorithms in the search for optimal configurations, with potential applications in machine learning and data analysis. The core mechanism centers around exploiting the unique properties of entangled quantum states to facilitate the discovery of highly correlated patterns, ultimately leading to improved model optimization. This research explores the theoretical foundations and practical implementation of DMQA, highlighting its potential for significant advancements in these fields. The paper concludes with a discussion of the algorithm's strengths, limitations, and future research directions.

title: Relational Transformers for Knowledge Graph Completion
abstract: Knowledge graph completion (KGC) is a crucial task in leveraging the wealth of information stored within knowledge graphs. Traditional approaches, such as graph convolutional networks (GCNs), often fall short in capturing the intricate, long-range dependencies inherent in these structures. This work introduces a novel approach, Relational Transformers, designed specifically for KGC. We propose an architecture based on the transformer model, adapted to effectively model relationships within a knowledge graph. The core idea is to utilize self-attention mechanisms to learn representations of entities and their connections, allowing the model to capture both local and global dependencies. We demonstrate that this approach can significantly improve the accuracy of predicting missing links compared to established methods. The model is trained to predict the existence (or absence) of a relationship between two entities given their connected neighbors. The key innovation lies in the ability of the transformer to inherently handle variable-length sequences and complex interactions, crucial for the irregular nature of knowledge graphs. The results presented here show the potential of relational transformers for robust and accurate knowledge graph completion.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Field: A Novel Computational Paradigm and Information Carrier
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of quantum entanglement information fields as a novel computational paradigm and information carrier, specifically targeted towards enhancing the efficiency of quantum computation and data transmission. The core concept centers around the utilization of quantum entanglement to facilitate novel calculations and data storage techniques. We explore a defined computational framework predicated on entanglement, detailing its mechanisms for manipulation and storage of quantum states. This research proposes a fundamentally different approach to quantum information processing, offering potential advancements beyond current quantum algorithms. The investigation focuses on the exploration of quantum state manipulation and information encoding through entangled states, aiming to unlock new capabilities in quantum computation.

title: Non-Euclidean Metric Learning for Data Distribution Analysis
abstract: This paper introduces a novel method for learning non-Euclidean metric spaces, offering a robust approach to data distribution analysis. Traditional metric learning methods often rely on assumptions about data distribution, limiting their applicability. We propose a deep learning framework that learns a metric space invariant to local transformations, enabling the automated detection of unusual data patterns. The core mechanism involves a novel neural network architecture designed to effectively capture complex data dependencies and identify deviations from expected patterns. This approach overcomes limitations of existing methods by offering greater flexibility and adaptability in analyzing data distributions. The paper details the architecture, training procedure, and initial results demonstrating the effectiveness of this method in identifying anomalies and patterns.

title: Task-Guided Multi-UAV Cooperative Multi-Target Tracking with Gaussian Process-Based Value Correction
abstract: The cooperative tracking of multiple ground targets by multiple UAVs remains challenging under partial observability, limited communication, and obstacle constraints, owing to complex target association, difficult task handover, strong coupling among low-level continuous control decisions, and unstable critic value estimation. To address these issues, this paper proposes a hierarchical-guidance and Gaussian-process-corrected multi-agent proximal policy optimization method, termed HGP-MAPPO. Built upon the centralized-training and decentralized-execution paradigm, HGP-MAPPO introduces low-frequency task-guidance signals derived from target-association information, task handover and recovery cues, task priorities, and desired observation geometry. These guidance signals are incorporated as conditional inputs into the low-level actor–critic framework, thereby reducing the policy learning difficulty in jointly handling target tracking, occlusion recovery, obstacle avoidance, and smooth control. Moreover, to alleviate local estimation bias in the neural-network critic under complex partially observable conditions, a Gaussian-process-based residual correction mechanism is designed. Specifically, the posterior mean is used to compensate for value residuals, while the posterior uncertainty adaptively regulates the correction intensity, improving the stability of value evaluation and policy optimization. A sparse inducing-point approximation is adopted to control the training-stage computational cost, while the Gaussian-process module is removed during decentralized execution and, therefore, introduces no additional online inference overhead. Experiments are conducted in standard-obstacle and densely obstructed multi-UAV multi-target tracking scenarios, with DDPG-MHSA, MAPPO, MADDPG, and MATD3 adopted as baselines. The experimental results demonstrate that HGP-MAPPO achieves faster training convergence, higher average episode rewards, and improved target retention rates. It also effectively reduces UAV–target distance fluctuations and the mean absolute temporal-difference (TD) error. Ablation studies further confirm the contributions of task-guidance signals, Gaussian-process residual correction, and uncertainty-aware weighting to cooperative tracking performance and training stability.

title: Affect-aware conversational adaptation in mixed reality procedural tasks
abstract: Abstract Conversational agents based on Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly explored in eXtended Reality (XR) applications that require real-time guidance during task execution. In task-oriented XR environments, conversational support must remain responsive and integrated with the ongoing activity, minimizing interruptions in user interaction. Although affect-aware adaptation has been proposed as a possible strategy to improve interaction quality, its impact in immersive task-oriented scenarios remains unclear. This paper presents a mixed-reality conversational system that integrates voice interaction, LLM-driven dialogue, and prosody-based affect-aware adaptation. The system adopts a modular client–server architecture with parallel semantic and affective processing pipelines, enabling emotion-related cues inferred from vocal prosody to be incorporated without interrupting conversational flow. The system was evaluated through a between-subjects study involving 40 participants performing a guided chemical procedure within a mixed-reality laboratory scenario. Participants interacted with either an affect-adaptive or a non-adaptive version of the conversational agent. The evaluation combined standardized questionnaires, behavioral metrics extracted from interaction logs, and qualitative feedback. Results showed that the affect-adaptive condition produced greater perceived usability scores compared to the non-adaptive condition. Participants interacting with the adaptive agent also required longer task completion times and engaged in a higher number of conversational turns. No significant differences emerged for overall workload between the two conditions. Qualitative findings further suggested that affect-aware adaptation made the interaction feel more natural and supportive.

title: PAC-Private Autoregressive Generation: Calibrating Noise to Ensemble Disagreement
abstract: Language models adapted on private text are often served through APIs, so privacy leakage occurs through generated outputs rather than exposed weights. Private prediction protects these releases. Methods such as PMixED incur privacy cost at each release and increasingly rely on the public model over long horizons. PAC privacy instead calibrates noise to output variability across possible secrets, adding less noise when predictions are stable. To our knowledge, PAC-private prediction has not previously been extended from classification to autoregressive generation. We construct $m=128$ overlapping worlds from the private corpus, with each record appearing in exactly $m/2$ worlds, and train one adapter per world over a frozen public model. The realized world is the secret. At each token, the public model defines a candidate set, the worlds vote, and their posterior-weighted disagreement determines the PAC noise; unanimity requires no calibration noise. We prove $I(S;Y_{1:T}) \leq I(S;H_T) \leq bT$. Our contributions are extending PAC privacy to autoregressive generation, handling adaptive self-generated contexts, and introducing coupled decoding that preserves privacy accounting while avoiding greedy degeneration. On WikiText-103 with GPT-2-small, we retain 74% of the fine-tuning gain at a per-token budget of $2^{-32}$, while membership-inference success is bounded by 51.08% after $10^6$ tokens; posterior-entropy estimates of leakage are roughly 17% of the charged budget. Inference privacy is not content protection: even when membership advantage on a memorized canary is indistinguishable from zero, the canary is emitted at the same rate. Against PMixED under matched membership-inference bounds on the same data universe and test set, we retain 98% of non-private headroom from $10^2$ to $10^6$ tokens, versus at most 56%, with no crossover.

title: Injected and Leaked: Actively Inducing Side-Channel Leakage Using Electromagnetic Injection and Hardware Nonlinearity
abstract: Electromagnetic (EM) side-channel leakage and injection are typically treated as distinct physical phenomena, threatening data confidentiality and integrity respectively. This work investigates how EM injection can be used to amplify side-channel leakage that is otherwise infeasible. We introduce a novel framework for Injection-Induced EM Side Channels to enable integrated, closed-loop EM security analysis. Our theoretical modeling and experimental measurements reveal that nonlinear hardware components, such as ubiquitous amplifiers, analog-to-digital converters, and power converters, can modulate secret electrical signals onto an injected EM carrier and thus upconvert low-frequency secrets into measurable EM emissions. By tuning the injection frequency and amplitude, adversaries gain the ability to actively shape the effective spectrum and entropy of the resulting leakage. We design InjectEave attack and demonstrate eavesdropping on the audio played through wired and wireless headphones from up to 30 m away with accessible RF equipment, as well as in through-wall scenarios, and characterize injection-induced EM leakage of other low-frequency secrets such as power consumption of smart home devices and analog sensor inputs. Case studies further demonstrate how the proposed techniques enable closed-loop eavesdropping and manipulation of landline-phone conversations. Finally, we analyze the broader security challenges and mitigations.

title: SiLR: Structure-Preserving Admission and Process Reward for LLM Tool Agents
abstract: A runtime gate for an LLM tool agent is usually cast as a filter. In a ReAct loop a rejected proposal is followed by another at the same state, so the gate is a search operator over the proposal stream whose admission criterion shapes which trajectories are reachable. We study post-violation recovery admission, where progress must be admitted while the system is still in violation, and identify the scalar projection trap: an aggregate-score gate accepts a locally improving proposal and commits the trajectory to a plateau. SiLR instead shadow-executes each proposal and admits it under a product order over the branch-level violation state (overloaded-branch support and per-branch severity). We prove that no scalar surrogate is sound for this order, so the failure is representational, not a matter of threshold tuning. On mined Gym-ANM scenarios, SiLR recovers 21/21 multi-action episodes against 0/21 for terminal and 9/21 for the best scalar gate, significant across the full 24-scenario benchmark. The terminal-versus-structured dichotomy holds across three model families and in CityLearn. Because admission rests on deterministic simulation, the LLM lies outside the trust boundary: a magnitude-redistribution attack that defeats both scalar and support-only baselines is contained only by the full per-branch predicate. With two constraint families active, every tested scalar projection admits physically unsafe actions; support-only admits the largest fraction (63.2% of 42,410; product order 0). In the hardest dual-family traces, scalar gates recover only through that unsafe class. Reused as a GRPO process reward, it outperforms its count projection in every mined scenario and is the only tested reward whose ungated policy exceeds the untrained base (0.844 vs. 0.778). Scalar projection loses the violation geometry at both design points; only the full product order is structurally sufficient.

title: Hierarchical Feedback Loops in Bayesian Inference for Complex Systems
abstract: This paper investigates the application of hierarchical feedback loops within Bayesian inference to enhance the accuracy and robustness of predictions for complex systems. Traditional Bayesian methods often struggle with convergence issues and sensitivity to initial conditions. We propose a novel framework where higher-level nodes provide feedback to lower-level nodes, creating a layered structure that facilitates more stable and reliable predictions. The core mechanism leverages a tiered approach to inference, allowing for the iterative refinement of predictions through a series of interconnected feedback cycles. This approach addresses limitations of current approaches by offering a more adaptable and resilient system capable of handling the inherent complexity of real-world problems. The paper demonstrates the efficacy of this framework through a series of simulations, showcasing improvements in prediction accuracy and robustness across various scenarios.

title: ##混沌动力学自适应算法
abstract: This paper investigates the application of a novel algorithm, termed the "混沌动力学自适应算法" (CDA), to optimize complex systems, with a particular focus on financial markets and biological evolution. The algorithm leverages the principles of chaos theory and adaptive algorithms to dynamically adjust parameters, enabling the system to respond effectively to changing conditions. This approach addresses the limitations of traditional optimization methods by incorporating inherent unpredictability and self-organization. The core mechanism revolves around a dynamic parameter adjustment process guided by the chaotic dynamics of the system being optimized. The research demonstrates the effectiveness of the CDA in achieving optimal solutions and rapid adaptation in challenging scenarios.

title: Quantum Machine Learning in Noise Matrix Optimization
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) offers a paradigm shift in machine learning, potentially surpassing classical approaches due to quantum phenomena. A critical challenge in many QML applications is the need to effectively manage noise within the model parameters, particularly in training datasets with high dimensionality. This paper explores the application of a novel noise matrix optimization algorithm, specifically tailored for QML, leveraging quantum properties to enhance model accuracy and stability. We propose a method that utilizes quantum superposition and entanglement to explore the parameter space more efficiently, leading to improved generalization performance. The core mechanism focuses on manipulating the noise matrix through quantum rotations and entanglement to achieve a more nuanced and robust optimization. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and preliminary experiments, highlighting its potential to significantly improve model performance in specific scenarios. The paper concludes with a discussion of future research directions and the implications of this quantum optimization technique for the field of machine learning.

title: falluck2025/prenary-math-lean-complex: Day15 v1.0.1 偏元数学— 复数域 ε · Lean 4 形式化验证
abstract: 声明:本文工作尚未得到独立实验验证,全部结论均为形式化验证层面的初步结果。 偏元数学·复数域 ε · Lean 4 形式化验证 Prenary Mathematics · Complex-Domain ε · Lean 4 Formal Verification 摘要:本文在 Lean 4 中对偏元数学的"复数域 ε"进行形式化验证,覆盖三步——① 复数加法留差(z ⊕ ε = z + ε);② 复数乘性旋转(z ⊗ ε = z · e^ε);③ 破群律的额外留差结构(群律破坏 + 同态破坏)。全部定理通过 Lean 内核 No goals 与 Comparator 独立二次验证,且 ε=0 时退化为经典复数运算。——老陈与AI的深夜实验室 发布 请笑纳—— Abstract: This repository formalizes "complex-domain ε" in prenary mathematics using Lean 4, covering three steps: (1) complex additive residue z ⊕ ε = z + ε; (2) complex multiplicative rotation z ⊗ ε = z · e^ε; (3) the extra-residue structure that breaks group law (group-law breaking + homomorphism breaking). All theorems pass Lean kernel No goals and Comparator independent verification, degenerating to classical complex arithmetic when ε = 0. — Published by Lao Chen & AI's Late Night Lab. title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Persistent Memory
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to persistent memory leveraging the principles of quantum entanglement. The core idea is to utilize entangled qubit states to create a memory system exhibiting inherent persistence and resilience to data corruption surpassing the limitations of conventional storage technologies. The system operates on a self-correcting algorithm continuously observing and manipulating the entangled qubits. This manipulation is driven by quantum decoherence properties, encoding redundancy and performing error correction without relying on explicit quantum error correction codes. The system's unique advantage lies in directly addressing decoherence through entanglement-driven self-organization, achieving true persistent storage at the quantum level. This approach fundamentally shifts the paradigm from actively correcting errors to passively allowing the system to self-organize and maintain data integrity through the inherent properties of entanglement and decoherence. Mathematical formulations detailing the core concepts and operational principles are presented. The system promises significantly enhanced data storage density, reliability, and resistance to environmental noise, representing a critical step toward practical quantum memory.

title: Self-Correcting Neural Networks via Adaptive Learning Rates and Regularization
abstract: Training deep neural networks often faces challenges related to instability and poor generalization due to the accumulation of errors during the learning process. This paper introduces a novel self-correcting neural network architecture designed to mitigate these issues. The core concept involves establishing a feedback loop that monitors the network's error signal and dynamically adjusts both learning rates and regularization parameters. This adaptive control mechanism aims to minimize error accumulation and promote more stable and effective training. The proposed approach offers a potential solution to the inherent instability of neural networks and contributes to improved model performance. The system utilizes a recurrent neural network (RNN) to process the error signal and generate adjustments to the network's hyperparameters. Mathematical formulations detail the adaptive learning rate and regularization parameter adjustment process. The overall impact is a network exhibiting enhanced robustness and generalization capabilities.

title: Contextualized Memory Networks with Hierarchical Semantic Decomposition
abstract: This paper introduces a novel memory network architecture designed to address the challenges of long-term dependency modeling in neural networks. The core idea is to integrate hierarchical semantic decomposition with contextualized memory access. Each memory unit is associated with a multi-level semantic representation, allowing the network to query memories based on increasingly abstract contextual cues. This approach enables more efficient and nuanced information retrieval, leading to improved performance in tasks requiring the capture of complex, long-range relationships. The proposed architecture is evaluated through theoretical analysis and conceptual design, highlighting its potential benefits and outlining future research directions. The key contribution lies in the synergistic combination of hierarchical semantic representation and contextualized memory access, offering a fundamentally new approach to memory network design.

title: Quantum Entanglement Probability Model
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, presents a significant challenge for practical quantum computing. Precise simulation of entangled states is crucial for developing robust quantum algorithms. This paper explores a novel model, the Quantum Entanglement Probability Model (QEMP), designed to capture the intricate probabilistic nature of entanglement and translate this into computational optimization for quantum computation. We propose a framework wherein entanglement probabilities directly influence the computational complexity of quantum circuits, enabling a more efficient design process. This model leverages a connection between entanglement and circuit complexity to achieve this transformation.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Multi-Scale Algorithm for Quantum Computing
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic adaptive multi-scale algorithm for quantum computing. Traditional approaches often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the model's ability to accurately capture the complexities of quantum systems. Our algorithm leverages the dynamic adjustment of quantum computation scales to provide a more precise and efficient modeling and analysis of complex system behavior. The core mechanism involves an optimization algorithm that dynamically adjusts the quantum system's parameters to enhance the representation of system dynamics. This results in improved accuracy and resilience compared to traditional methods. The proposed algorithm has the potential to significantly advance the field of quantum computing by enabling more sophisticated simulations and analysis.

title: 基于自适应的机器学习的非线性模型优化
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for non-linear model optimization based on adaptive machine learning. Traditional optimization methods often rely on fixed parameters, limiting the potential for improved generalization. Our proposed approach dynamically adjusts model parameters using a machine learning model, enabling automated optimization and enhanced model performance. We explore a specific implementation leveraging a stochastic gradient descent algorithm with a dynamically updated learning rate, demonstrating significant improvements in both training speed and model accuracy across a range of datasets. The core mechanism focuses on leveraging the model's internal state to guide optimization, resulting in a more robust and adaptable optimization process. This work provides a foundation for more efficient and versatile model training.

title: Opportunities and challenges of generative AI in the research lifecycle
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly being explored and adopted across the research lifecycle, from idea generation and literature discovery to data analysis, manuscript preparation, and editorial and peer-review processes. This perspective provides an overview of AI’s role across the stages of scientific research. We describe emerging tools and workflows, illustrating how AI can assist researchers by aggregating and synthesizing a large body of work across various domains, supporting methodological implementation, and facilitating communication and publication. We also discuss their shortcomings, including surface-level reasoning, the fabrication of plausible but incorrect outputs, and the challenges posed by the fact that researchers new to a field may not know which questions to ask or which nuances to interrogate. In addition, we discuss recent advances toward more agentic and end-to-end AI systems, highlighting both their technical feasibility and the challenges they pose for validation, oversight, and responsible use. For each stage of the research lifecycle, we outline key limitations of current AI systems and propose practical considerations, what researchers should and should not do to support rigorous and ethical integration of AI into scientific workflows. This integration requires coordinated frameworks across the ecosystem. Journals, funding agencies, universities, and policymakers play essential roles in defining standards for transparency and accountability, while individual researchers remain responsible for methodological rigor and validity of reported results.

title: Stop the spark detecting violence instigating Bangla text using ViolenceBanglaBERT
abstract: Abstract Due to the low cost and widespread availability of the internet and digital devices, the utilization of social networks is rapidly increasing. Therefore, in recent years, a group of individuals from different religions and cultural backgrounds has used social network platforms to promote misinformation and hatred, which has instigated communal violence and devastating consequences. Regarding this concerning rise of communal violence instigated through social media texts, this study presents a comprehensive benchmarking and optimization framework of multiple deep learning and transformer-based models for violence-instigating Bangla text classification. A wide range of embedding methods, deep learning architectures, transformer-based models, and existing approaches are systematically evaluated under a unified experimental framework. To address class imbalance, data augmentation via back-translation is applied to improve generalization. The experimental results illustrate that the proposed ViolenceBanglaBERT model, a fine-tuned version of a transformer-based classifier, achieved a Macro F1-score of 0.75 on the test set, outperforming other classifiers and existing approaches. The source code used in this study can be accessed at https://github.com/prosenjit-ch/SS-VIBTI .

title: From Monolithic Blending to Agentic Orchestration: Dynamic Response for Conversational Assistants at Scale
abstract: Conversational assistants can blend retrieval, action selection, escalation, and wording in a single model path, or separate those roles. We report a production migration of a customer-support assistant at a large accommodation marketplace (millions of conversations per month, 11 languages, 10-second P90). Dynamic Response (DR) replaces a single Qwen3-235B-A22B blended responder with a bounded ReAct orchestrator over typed tools plus a smaller generator that writes from a backend-validated context contract. Because the migration also changed prompts, alignment, and serving, we attribute each effect to its cause and claim as architecture effects only those measured on identical replayed turns: typed entity selection moves the reservation selector to a precision-first operating point (precision 8.3% to 89.1%, recall 75.2% to 67.3%), and typed action IDs with a membership check remove observed structured-action hallucination (2.14% to 0.0%). A low-ramp A/B test reproduces the replay escalation reductions: hard-escalation responses fall from 5.60% to 3.08% and soft-escalation responses from 9.56% to 2.49%, while production handoff volume holds roughly steady; self-solve is directional (+5.1 points, 95% CI [-2, +12]). Serving optimizations cut orchestrator P90 latency from 3.87s to 2.24s on a GPU footprint reduced by roughly one-third, and self-hosting reduces estimated annual model-serving cost by more than an order of magnitude.

title: From Matrices to Morphisms II: Examples of Computational Categories in MATLAB and Octave
abstract: This article develops the notion of a computational category, motivated by the observation that many mathematical structures occurring in scientific computing already admit concrete algorithmic representations. Finite sets, finite-dimensional vector spaces, relations, and graphs may all be represented through elementary MATLAB and Octave data structures such as indexing vectors, matrices, logical arrays, and sparse matrices. The central idea is that a category may often be described through a category of canonical representatives indexed by the natural numbers. This viewpoint leads naturally to representative categories whose objects are dimensions and whose morphisms are finite computational data structures. The resulting framework unifies several examples, including matrix categories, index categories, categories of column spaces, row-based models of finite sets, and categories combining finite subsets with finite-dimensional vector spaces through mixed morphisms. The paper also introduces computational categories with distinguished non-finite representatives, extending the finite setting while retaining concrete coordinate descriptions. Throughout, categorical constructions are interpreted algorithmically and implemented using standard MATLAB and Octave operations. The work contributes to a computational perspective on category theory and, conversely, to a categorical understanding of matrix-oriented scientific computing.

title: A Cost-Aware Agentic Architecture for NL-to-SQL over Nested Enterprise Schemas, with a New Benchmark
abstract: Natural-language-to-SQL systems have ad- vanced rapidly on academic benchmarks, yet production enterprise schemas exhibit graph- like, semi-structured, deeply nested structure that current benchmarks do not measure. We make two complementary contributions. First, we introduce the DevRev NL2SQL bench- mark: 900 execution-verified queries with nested-type and link-graph structure, accom- panied by the Semantic Depth Score (SDS), a schema-agnostic rubric for analytical reasoning depth. Second, we present a cost-aware single- generation agentic architecture whose schema- selection, metadata-retrieval, and error-repair components are designed for the requirements this regime imposes. On the DevRev NL2SQL benchmark the system attains 91.7% answer correctness, a margin of 54.6 percentage points over the next-best baseline; on the Spider 2.0 Snowflake public dataset, it is competitive with leading systems at a single-generation operating point.

title: Quantum Information Topological Field Theory
abstract: Quantum information theory has long been considered a promising avenue for advancing computational capabilities, particularly in the realm of quantum computing. However, existing quantum computing paradigms often rely on the manipulation of discrete quantum states and the execution of specific quantum gates. This research proposes a novel theoretical framework, the Quantum Information Topological Field Theory (QITFT), which explicitly integrates quantum entanglement with topological fields, offering a fundamentally new approach to computation. We aim to explore how the interplay between these two phenomena can lead to enhanced computational properties and a potential expansion of the quantum computing landscape. This work focuses on the core mechanisms of constructing a quantum computation process centered around the exploitation of quantum entanglement and topological field alignment. The current design incorporates a quantum entanglement-induced topological field formation, which is hypothesized to yield enhanced computational capabilities. This theory represents a departure from traditional quantum computing approaches, potentially addressing long-standing challenges and opening new avenues for algorithmic design.

title: Adaptive Quantum Machine Learning Parameter Adjustment Strategy Optimization
abstract: This paper investigates the application of quantum machine learning (QML) to parameter adjustment within the training process of classical machine learning models. Traditional parameter tuning methods often rely on fixed adjustments, failing to effectively leverage complex, dynamic information derived from model training. We propose a novel approach that leverages quantum algorithms to dynamically adjust model parameters based on both model training error and gradient information, promoting more robust and accurate model performance. This method integrates quantum error analysis into the parameter adjustment process, offering a fundamentally new approach to optimization. The research explores the potential of quantum mechanics to enhance the efficiency and adaptability of parameter optimization, potentially surpassing the limitations of classical methods. This work focuses on the design and implementation of a QML-based parameter adjustment strategy, incorporating quantum algorithms for error assessment and dynamic parameter refinement. We demonstrate the efficacy of this approach through simulations and preliminary experiments, highlighting its potential to improve model generalization and robustness.

title: Ledger Vouching: Grounding Someone Else's Agent over the Wire
abstract: Tool-using LLM agents ship reports whose load-bearing values — numbers, identifiers, quantities — are frequently fabricated in-head: across two model generations, each measured under its own value-dense reporting demand, the per-token fabrication rate collapsed while the rate of episodes shipping at least one unverified value stayed at 75–81%. We present ledger vouching: an OpenAI-protocol proxy (the ledger voucher), adopted by changing one base_url line, compiles everything it observes on the wire into an observation ledger and deterministically vouches every load-bearing value in its extracted class (digit-bearing tokens: numbers, dates, prices, quantities, alphanumeric identifiers) in an agent's terminal answer to that ledger — no harness cooperation, and no verdict authority for any model: the ledger voucher itself enumerates verified candidate origins by reverse lookup against the ledger, and the model only selects among them for the audit trail. Enforcement is a three-mode ladder — flag, block (honest refusal), and retry (a close-gate keep-alive that pushes the agent to ground its own answer inside the protocol) — with a mandatory explicit fail posture; the guarantee is existence-semantics provenance, never correctness, with its residual refusal families stated and measured. Across two environments and two model generations we measure: transparency from byte level to operational (Δ = 0.000); zero unverified-value shipping in block mode (0/16 and 0/16 in live runs across generations under the enforced predicate, with the refusal cost quantified alongside; 814/814 fabricated-token recall against a privileged oracle in replay); honest, graceful degradation of retry on weak models alongside one-round convergence on a capable one; deterministic cost amplification (1.0×/2.0×/3.0×); and 13% directional agreement with an LLM judge that prefers fabricated answers in 10% of pairs. A companion paper reports that preference training on the same deterministic verifier's labels failed to reduce fabrication while a zero-training environment contract succeeded; the prescription our combined evidence supports is contract plus deterministic enforcement at the boundary.

title: Title: Quantum Decoherence Shielding (QDS)
abstract: Quantum Decoherence is a significant and persistent challenge in the field of quantum computing, hindering the development of practical quantum systems. This research investigates a novel shielding technique, Quantum Field Resonance Shielding (QDS), to actively mitigate this issue. We propose a method to generate a localized region of reduced decoherence through the precise manipulation of quantum fields, offering a proactive solution to the fundamental obstacle to quantum information processing. This work details the theoretical framework, implementation steps, and experimental validation of the QDS protocol, demonstrating its potential to significantly enhance the stability and performance of quantum systems. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the underlying principles and potential applications of QDS.

evidence.title: Title: Quantum Decoherence Shielding (QDS)
evidence.abstract: Quantum Decoherence is a significant and persistent challenge in the field of quantum computing, hindering the development of practical quantum systems. This research investigates a novel shielding technique, Quantum Field Resonance Shielding (QDS), to actively mitigate this issue. We propose a method to generate a localized region of reduced decoherence through the precise manipulation of quantum fields, offering a proactive solution to the fundamental obstacle to quantum information processing. This work details the theoretical framework, implementation steps, and experimental validation of the QDS protocol, demonstrating its potential to significantly enhance the stability and performance of quantum systems. This paper presents a comprehensive analysis of the underlying principles and potential applications of QDS.

title: Dynamic Quantum Computing Resource Allocation and Scheduling Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to dynamic quantum computing resource allocation and scheduling, addressing the limitations of static resource management in the field. The core claim is that real-time monitoring of quantum resource utilization combined with the inherent characteristics of quantum algorithms can lead to optimized dynamic allocation and scheduling, ultimately boosting quantum computing efficiency. The proposed mechanism leverages reinforcement learning (RL) to learn an optimal resource allocation policy. The RL agent adapts to the specific requirements of quantum algorithms, considering factors such as the number of qubits and their entanglement level. The algorithm aims to minimize execution time and maximize resource utilization. This research contributes to a more flexible and efficient utilization of scarce quantum computing resources, a critical factor in the advancement of quantum computation. The key performance indicator is the reduction in the average execution time of quantum algorithms, compared to static allocation strategies. The theoretical framework is built upon queuing theory and stochastic optimization techniques.

title: Algorithmic Bias Detection and Mitigation in Federated Learning
abstract: Federated learning (FL) presents a promising paradigm for training machine learning models on decentralized data, preserving data privacy. However, this approach is increasingly recognized to be vulnerable to algorithmic bias. The inherent diversity and potential imbalances within the data contributed by numerous clients can significantly impact the fairness and equity of the resulting global model. This paper investigates the propagation and amplification of biases in federated learning systems. We propose a framework for detecting and mitigating these biases by integrating differential privacy and fairness constraints into the training process. The core claim is that FL systems are inherently susceptible to bias propagation. The proposed mechanism involves monitoring model performance across client subgroups, quantifying bias metrics, and adjusting the training process to enforce fairness. This work contributes to the development of more robust and trustworthy FL systems, paving the way for responsible and equitable AI applications.

title: Dynamic Probability Field Models (DPF) – Extended
abstract: Dynamic Probability Field Models (DPF) represent a powerful framework for probabilistic modeling, enabling prediction by dynamically adjusting probability distributions based on environmental changes. This paper explores an extended DPF concept that introduces a "variable parameter" mechanism, enhancing its adaptability and precision in complex environments. We outline the core principles, theoretical foundation, and potential applications of this enhanced DPF, emphasizing the novelty of the variable parameter approach and its implications for improved predictive accuracy.

title: 自适应拓扑的量子几何验证
abstract: This paper investigates the application of adaptive topology in quantum geometry to validate quantum systems, offering a novel approach to quantum computation verification. We propose a framework leveraging quantum computation's inherent properties to explore the complex topology that might emerge in quantum systems, ultimately providing a more robust and efficient quantum verification tool. The core claim is that establishing a self-adaptive topology in quantum geometry will yield a more accurate and reliable assessment of quantum system behavior, thereby enhancing the quality of quantum computations. This research focuses on utilizing quantum algorithms to identify and quantify topological features, offering a shift towards a more systematic and predictive verification process. This work introduces a new methodology for quantum geometry validation, incorporating adaptive techniques to improve the robustness and accuracy of verification procedures.

title: Algorithmic Co-evolution in Evolutionary Computation
abstract: This paper introduces a novel algorithmic framework, Algorithmic Co-evolution, designed to enhance the performance of evolutionary algorithms by incorporating a feedback loop between the algorithm's parameters and the outcomes of previous iterations. Traditional evolutionary approaches often rely on a single, fixed evolutionary process, limiting their capacity to explore complex solution spaces and achieve optimal performance. We propose a system where the algorithm iteratively refines its parameters based on the results of previous steps, fostering a self-improvement mechanism. This approach, termed Co-evolution, creates a continuous feedback loop that surpasses the inherent limitations of traditional methods, leading to improved solutions for complex optimization problems. The core mechanism centers around dynamically adjusting the problem's constraints and objective function based on the algorithm's output, driving a self-evolving solution space. This paper presents a detailed exploration of the Co-evolution algorithm, its implementation, and preliminary results on a challenging problem involving multi-objective optimization.

title: Title: Bayesian Network for Dynamical Systems in High-Dimensional Space
abstract: This research investigates the application of Bayesian Networks (BNs) to model and predict the evolution of complex, multi-variable dynamical systems within high-dimensional spaces. Traditional probabilistic models often fall short in effectively capturing the intricate dependencies and inherent uncertainty present in such systems. We propose a novel Bayesian Network architecture that explicitly models uncertainty as a latent variable, leveraging variational inference for efficient exploration of the network's state space. This approach offers a more robust and principled framework for handling high dimensionality, leading to improved prediction accuracy and a deeper understanding of the underlying dynamics. The core mechanism centers around a dynamically updated latent variable that influences the probabilities of different future states, ensuring a continuous representation of uncertainty. We demonstrate the efficacy of this method through a series of simulations and analysis, showcasing its ability to accurately predict system behavior in challenging high-dimensional scenarios.

title: Quantum Entanglement-Based Calculation Model
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a perplexing phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holds the potential to revolutionize computation. This paper explores the design of a novel calculation model predicated on entanglement, aiming to accelerate complex calculations through the exploitation of this quantum property. We introduce the concept of 'entangled states' as a core mechanism, utilizing their unique characteristics to facilitate parallel processing and enhanced computational efficiency. The model's core claim centers around the ability to leverage entanglement to significantly reduce computational complexity compared to traditional methods. This research will detail the proposed model's architecture, the mathematical framework underpinning its operation, and preliminary results demonstrating its potential for advanced calculations. We will also address challenges and future directions for this burgeoning field.

title: 基于动态图的逻辑推演算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to logical reasoning, utilizing a dynamic graph representation to enhance efficiency in handling large-scale inference problems. Traditional logical reasoning algorithms often struggle with the complexity of large instances. Our algorithm leverages a dynamic graph to simulate the reasoning process, employing self-adaptive mechanisms to optimize performance. This work introduces a method to dynamically adjust the graph structure and reasoning steps, significantly improving the scalability and efficiency of logical inference. The core mechanism focuses on the iterative refinement of the graph based on the current state of the inference, resulting in a more robust and adaptable system. The proposed algorithm offers a promising avenue for addressing challenges in complex logical tasks.

title: 基于深度学习的非线性信号处理的动态泛化模型
abstract: This paper explores the application of deep learning to dynamic signal processing, focusing on the development of a novel model designed to effectively mitigate generalization errors across diverse datasets. Traditional signal processing methods often rely on static models, limiting their adaptability to complex, non-linear data distributions. We propose a dynamic, adaptive deep learning framework that learns robust representations and dynamically adjusts its parameters to better suit the specific characteristics of each input. The core of this approach lies in leveraging deep neural networks to automatically extract and refine key features, thereby enabling more robust and accurate signal processing. This research addresses a critical challenge in signal analysis – the need for models capable of handling complex, non-linear data – and presents a promising pathway toward improved performance in a variety of real-world applications.

title: A Multi-Strategy Enhanced Crested Porcupine Optimizer with Targeted Defense Mechanism Improvement for Global Optimization
abstract: Metaheuristic algorithms are widely used to solve complex optimization problems, but the trade-off between exploration and exploitation often limits their performance. The Crested Porcupine Optimizer (CPO) employs four bio-inspired defense mechanisms and achieves competitive performance, but it still tends to converge prematurely, initialize populations poorly, and rely on static parameters that cannot adapt to different phases. This paper proposes a Multi-Strategy Enhanced Crested Porcupine Optimizer (MSCPO) with four phase-targeted enhancement strategies: (1) Kent Chaos Opposition-Based Learning Initialization (KCOL) improves the initial population distribution through chaotic-weighted reflection; (2) Arctic Puffin Optimization (APO)-Inspired Dual-Modal Evasion (APO-DME) reduces dependence on the global best solution and increases population diversity through dual-mode differential perturbation; (3) Adaptive Dual-Differential Perturbation (ADDP) refines the search by combining population diversity and elite guidance information; (4) Periodic Dynamic Adaptive Perturbation (PDAP) enhances exploitation through periodic trigonometric perturbation and a fitness-conditioned update rule. These strategies interact across the optimization process to strengthen each defense mechanism at the appropriate phase. On the CEC 2017 and CEC 2022 benchmark suites, MSCPO achieves the best overall mean rank among all compared algorithms, with an overall rank of 2.638 on CEC 2017 and 2.375 on CEC 2022. A full-factorial ablation over all 16 strategy combinations confirms that each strategy contributes positively: removing any single strategy degrades the overall mean rank, and the complete MSCPO achieves the best mean rank (3.34), significantly outperforming all single-strategy variants (Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p < 0.001). To verify the practical applicability of MSCPO, the algorithm is further applied to three engineering design problems: step-cone pulley design, hydrostatic thrust bearing design, and robotic gripper design. MSCPO ranks first on the hydrostatic thrust bearing problem, second on the step-cone pulley problem, and third on the robotic gripper problem. Future work will explore adaptive population sizing to further improve the scalability of MSCPO on very high-dimensional problems.

title: Tight Lower Bounds for State Tomography with Limited Entanglement
abstract: We study state tomography when each measurement acts on at most $k$ fresh copies and no quantum memory is retained between blocks. We prove a lower bound matching the upper bound in [arXiv:2510.07788]. Thus the copy complexity of estimating an arbitrary $d$-dimensional state to trace distance $ε$ is, up to absolute constant factors, $\max\{d^3/(\sqrt{k}ε^2),d^2/ε^2\}$ for every $k$ and all sufficiently small $ε$. This removes the earlier restriction that $k$ be small as a function of the accuracy. The lower bound applies to arbitrary measurements within each block and adaptive choices between blocks. The lower bound already applies in a small neighborhood of any state whose smallest eigenvalue is of order $1/d$, even when the center is known. The main ingredient is a uniform Fisher information bound for one measurement block that depends only on the smallest eigenvalue of the state. The proof avoids the perturbative expansion responsible for the restriction in [arXiv:2402.16353]. Fano's inequality for metric balls and a log-Sobolev comparison between mutual and Fisher information then reduce the adaptive protocol to this block bound [arXiv:1607.00550, arXiv:1902.08582].

title: CPL: A Compact C-like Systems Language with Explicit Low-Level Control
abstract: This paper presents Cordell Programming Language (CPL), a compact C-like systems language that retains C's direct access to memory, layout, and machine interfaces while experimenting with a smaller grammar and selected conveniences from newer languages. Also this paper studies whether C-like are more convenient to use for compiler experiments than modern approaches and paradigms. While the language and compiler provide primitive values, pointers, arrays, containers with methods, unions, generic functions, overloads, entry-point and section control, system calls, and inline assembly, they do not provide high-level constructs such as classes, built-in methods, a standard library, or memory protection. The article describes the language design, compiler pipeline, target backends, static-analysis architecture, and OS-facing use cases, then evaluates the prototype backend with reproducible x86_64 and i386 microbenchmarks against C compiler baselines. The obtained results suggest that the compiler can produce code comparable to that produced by production compilers such as GCC and Clang, as well as by small compilers such as TinyC and SmallerC.

title: MMTClinic: Multimodal, Multilingual Time Series Question Answering and Reasoning Benchmark for Clinical Domain
abstract: Time-series data in clinical settings is crucial for capturing dynamic changes in a patient's health over time, enabling timely diagnosis, personalized treatment, and early detection of critical events. However, the development of clinically reliable and linguistically inclusive medical AI systems remains a significant challenge, primarily due to the lack of multimodal, multilingual, and time-series-grounded benchmarks that reflect the complexity of real-world clinical scenarios. To fill this gap, we present MMTClinic, a benchmark designed to evaluate large language models (LLMs) on complex reasoning and question-answering tasks involving clinical time-series. MMTClinic combines text, medical images, and multivariate physiological signals and includes 30,000 QA pairs (15,000 multiple choice questions (MCQs) and 15,000 open-ended questions) across five languages: English, Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, and Tamil. These questions cover three important clinical tasks---mortality prediction, heart rate forecasting, and SOFA score estimation. We evaluate 13 state-of-the-art LLMs in zero-shot, few-shot, and chain-of-thought settings. Our evaluation reveals notable differences in model performance across tasks, languages, and modalities, highlighting current limitations in clinical reasoning capabilities. MMTClinic provides a valuable resource for advancing multilingual, multimodal, and time-series-aware medical AI research. The dataset will be made publicly available on successful acceptance of the work.

title: A Study on The Impact of Generative AI on Investment Decision Making at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.
abstract: This study, titled "A Study on the Impact of Generative AI on Investment Decision Making at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd.," evaluates use case allocations, research analyst productivity gains, Assets Under Management (AUM) expansion, and financial feasibility of Generative AI (GenAI) integration in institutional wealth management and retail equity advisory. Wealth management firms face high research overhead, where equity report drafting represents 42% and portfolio chatbots account for 28% of GenAI applications. A five-year project lifecycle (2021-2025) of an enterprise GenAI research platform at Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd. is evaluated using capital budgeting parameters: Net Present Value (NPV), Internal Rate of Return (IRR), Payback Period (PBP), and Benefit-Cost Ratio (BCR). Quantitative analysis reveals that deploying a GenAI research copilot reduces valuation report preparation time to 2.1 hours compared to 18.5 hours under manual research. High research velocity supports advisory AUM growth to 21,800 Crores while expanding retail portfolio annual returns to 34.5%, lifting GenAI tool adoption to 92.4% and compressing decision latency to 1.2 hours by 2025. The financial model yields a positive NPV of 284.5 Crores and an IRR of 38.6%, far exceeding the 10% discount hurdle rate. The study concludes that investing in Generative AI copilot engines is highly viable, boosting equity research efficiency and retail investor portfolio alpha.

title: DPStatPrompt
abstract: This is a minimal implementation of our paper: Differentially Private Term Statistics for Efficient Synthetic Text Generation. The script automatically downloads AG News, WikiText-103, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.3, and RoBERTa-base from Hugging Face. It uses the first 4,000 AG News training examples from each class (16,000 total), builds the public vocabulary from WikiText, performs one record-level analytic-Gaussian release, generates 5,000 balanced news texts, and evaluates them over seeds 0, 1, and 2. title: Title: Parallel Algorithm for Quantum State Collapse Analysis
abstract: Quantum state collapse is a fundamental process in quantum mechanics, and its analysis is a critical task in quantum algorithm design and verification. Traditional methods struggle to handle the immense complexity of quantum systems due to the exponential growth of state space. This paper introduces a novel parallel algorithm designed to efficiently analyze the collapse of quantum states, utilizing distributed computing techniques to rapidly explore the vast state space and pinpoint key collapse pathways. The algorithm's core mechanism involves distributing the analysis across multiple cores and nodes, leveraging advanced quantum computing techniques to expedite the evaluation of various parameters. This approach promises to dramatically reduce computational time and enhance the ability to identify crucial collapse events, ultimately improving the robustness and reliability of quantum algorithms. This work addresses a long-standing challenge in quantum state collapse analysis and offers a promising pathway towards more efficient and scalable quantum system modeling.

abstract: Quantum Complexity Theory (QCT) offers a novel framework for verifying the correctness of complex mathematical proofs, moving beyond traditional verification methods reliant on computational complexity. This paper introduces a new protocol leveraging quantum entanglement to simultaneously assess multiple steps within a proof, dramatically increasing the probability of detecting subtle inconsistencies. The core mechanism involves creating entangled qubits to explore the proof space in a fundamentally different way, revealing logical errors with significantly enhanced precision. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a detailed analysis of a simplified example, highlighting its potential to revolutionize the verification process. The research explores the inherent challenges and opportunities presented by quantum mechanics in this domain, emphasizing the potential for a paradigm shift in mathematical assurance.

abstract: Quantum state transfer and mitigation are critical challenges in quantum computing, requiring efficient and robust methods to handle complex quantum systems. This research contributes to a fundamental shift in the design of quantum algorithms, offering a promising path toward more practical and reliable quantum computing.

The paper details the design of the Quantum Probability Logic system, its underlying mathematical principles, and its potential applications across diverse mathematical domains. We explore the advantages and challenges of this new methodology, emphasizing its capacity to provide a more dependable foundation for formal reasoning.

abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic quantum key distribution (QKD) protocol designed to enhance security by adapting to fluctuating environmental noise. Traditional QKD protocols often operate under the assumption of constant noise, which is rarely true in real-world scenarios. This protocol leverages quantum feedback control to monitor and respond to changes in the noise level, thereby improving key generation rates and overall security. The core mechanism involves dynamically adjusting key distribution parameters based on real-time noise measurements. The design addresses a critical limitation of existing protocols and offers a more robust and practical approach to secure key exchange. This work outlines the theoretical framework, key equations, and the proposed algorithm for this dynamic QKD protocol.

title: An Enhanced Newton Downhill Optimizer for High-Dimensional Optimization and Thermal–Pumped-Storage Economic Dispatch
abstract: The Newton Downhill Optimizer (NDO) provides a compact derivative-free search framework, but its random dimension mask, uniform treatment of individuals, and limited use of supplementary global-best candidates may restrict performance on high-dimensional problems. This study proposes an Enhanced Newton Downhill Optimizer (ENDO) that incorporates three mechanisms: an adaptive dimension mask, a DE/rand/2-based greedy mutation for inferior individuals, and dynamic-boundary opposition-based best guidance. ENDO was evaluated on the CEC2017 benchmark at 10, 30, 50, and 100 dimensions. The primary comparison involved nine representative optimizers, and an additional 100-dimensional comparison was conducted with six advanced optimizers. In the primary 100-dimensional tests, ENDO ranked first on 18 of 29 functions, remained among the top three on 26 functions, and achieved an average rank of 1.79. In the additional comparison, ENDO ranked third with an average rank of 3.52. Across the four dimensions, its average ranks were 1.79, 1.66, 1.38, and 1.79, indicating stable performance under changes in problem scale. ENDO was further applied to a 168-dimensional thermal–pumped-storage economic dispatch problem, where it achieved the lowest mean operating cost, the best average rank of 1.87, and a feasibility rate of 100% over 30 independent runs. Statistical analyses further supported the competitiveness of ENDO across the benchmark and engineering evaluations. These results show that ENDO improves the sustained search capability of NDO and provides competitive performance for complex high-dimensional and constrained optimization problems.

title: Advances in time-independent Hamiltonian simulation algorithms
abstract: Abstract Quantum simulation is a rapidly advancing field poised to revolutionize our understanding of complex quantum systems by harnessing the unique capabilities of quantum computers. In this review, we present a concise overview of key developments in quantum simulation algorithms, with a focus on time-independent digital Hamiltonian simulation of quantum dynamics. We review seminal methods—from traditional Trotter formulas to techniques such as truncated Taylor series combined with the linear combination of unitaries, and quantum signal processing. Additionally, we examine error analyses and recent innovations that enhance the efficiency and accuracy of quantum simulations.

title: Adaptive Cost-Sensitive Machine Learning for Autonomous Robot Navigation Failure Prediction: When Not All Errors Are Equal
abstract: Autonomous robot navigation failures differ not only in categorical severity but also in the physical context in which they occur. A near-miss at low speed under reliable sensing is not equivalent to the same event during rapid motion, close obstacle approach or degraded perception. This paper reframes navigation failure prediction as consequence-sensitive forecasting. We first establish a fixed baseline in which training weights are modulated by categorical severity, then introduce an adaptive extension defining a state-dependent consequence function combining severity with normalised velocity, obstacle proximity and sensing uncertainty, together with a risk-sensitivity term that rises as conditions deteriorate. We evaluate on 2,000 simulated differential-drive episodes (~1,000,000 timesteps) using episode-level GroupKFold, with external validation on the UCI SCITOS G5 dataset. Fixed weighting raises Logistic Regression high-severity recall from 0.851 to 0.985 and reduces missed consequence cost from 1,940 to 313; the adaptive extension reaches 0.998 and 82. Under matched false-positive conditions, however, the discriminative advantage is modest (0.986 versus 0.984), so most of the gain reflects a more conservative operating point rather than better ranking. The effect is consistent across all five folds and stable across a threefold span of context coefficients. Because the primary simulation produced no collisions, we add a controlled extension in which 108 of 600 episodes terminate in contact: collision recall rises from 0.850 to 0.966 (fixed) and 0.984 (adaptive), with missed collision cost falling from 1,000 to 105, at false-positive rates of 0.413 and 0.799, respectively. Context-dependent consequence modelling thus provides a principled mechanism for allocating conservatism by physical risk.

title: Fundamental Limits of Quantum Metrology Beyond Fixed Causal Order
abstract: Quantum metrology with indefinite causal order (ICO) has attracted intense interest due to its potential to surpass the limitations of conventional fixed-order strategies. A key open question is whether ICO can fundamentally enhance asymptotic precision scaling. In this work, we bridge this gap for the estimation of a single parameter encoded in $N$ identical uses of a finite-dimensional quantum channel. We first establish a universal Heisenberg-scaling upper bound for the full general ICO process-matrix class and show that for unitary channels its optimal quantum Fisher information (QFI) coincides exactly with that of parallel strategies. For noisy channels, a structurally refined bound shows that channels restricted to the standard quantum limit (SQL) under parallel strategies remain SQL-limited under general ICO strategies. Most significantly, an asymptotically tight (AT) bound is derived to close the remaining possibility of an asymptotic ICO advantage by showing that general ICO and optimal parallel strategies have exactly the same leading QFI coefficient in both the SQL and Heisenberg regimes. For the operationally motivated class of quantum circuits with quantum control of causal order, we further obtain an iterative constraint on finite-query precision whose asymptotic limit agrees with that of the AT bound. Our results clarify the ultimate role of indefinite causality as a metrological resource for quantum channel estimation.

title: Aplaud: Adaptive Personalized Low-Rank Decomposition for User-Specific LLM
abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of personalized survey response prediction using fine-tuned large language models (LLMs). This task poses unique challenges: limited per-user training data, scalability of model storage, and the need to exploit shared structure across survey questions. To address these issues, we propose Aplaud (Adaptive Personalized Low-rank and User-specific Nested Decomposition), a lightweight and scalable framework for LLM personalization. Aplaud extends the LoRA paradigm by separating adaptation into a frozen, shared low-rank basis and a compact user-specific correction, augmented with a rank-one residual for finer personalization. To further reduce per-user parameter cost and mitigate overfitting, the correction matrix can be factorized into an even lower-rank form. Empirical results demonstrate that Aplaud achieves efficient, scalable personalization across users while outperforming state-of-the-art LoRA-based personalized LLM approaches in both generalization and inference efficiency.

evidence.abstract: This paper presents a novel adaptive algorithm for optimization, leveraging the principles of a self-adaptive feedback loop. We introduce a 'Self-Adapting Feedback Loop' (SFL) mechanism that dynamically adjusts algorithm parameters to optimize complex systems, effectively mitigating uncertainty and enhancing robustness. The SFL approach significantly improves algorithm performance compared to static parameter tuning methods. This research emphasizes the algorithm's ability to adapt to changing environmental conditions, offering a more flexible and reliable solution for optimization problems. We explore the design, implementation, and performance evaluation of this algorithm, demonstrating its effectiveness in a simulated scenario.
